title: Evaluate deterministic documentation tooling candidates
objective: Evaluate DocGuard, Vale and lychee against the project's deterministic, bounded, zero-cost documentation-governance requirements before any external tooling is adopted or installed.
non_goals: install or execute third-party documentation tools
make any third-party tool a source of authorization
change project-state handoff or context-map schemas

forbidden_semantics: third-party documentation tool becomes current-state authority

required_invariants: candidate facts are bound to explicit release tags and exact source commits
only permissively licensed zero-cost candidates may receive a non-REJECT verdict
no candidate may override canonical project state handoff context map or generated status authority
network-dependent behavior cannot become mandatory per-change validation
new runtime or package-manager requirements cannot be silently introduced
evaluation verdicts are limited to ADOPT ADOPT_PARTIALLY COPY_PATTERN or REJECT
actual third-party execution or installation is deferred to a separately bounded follow-up AWU
acceptance_criteria: DocGuard release license Node runtime dependency pinned package dependency and Spec Kit overlap are recorded
Vale release license offline behavior and local-style requirement are recorded
lychee release dual license and offline local-link mode are recorded
each candidate has explicit benefits risks overlap network behavior rollback and proposed scope
evaluation identifies whether a follow-up benchmark/adoption AWU is justified
evaluator rejects floating versions missing source commits paid requirements authority conflicts and mandatory network checks
evaluation itself remains standard-library zero-cost and performs no external requests

done_when: all three candidates have deterministic auditable verdicts
no external documentation tool has been installed or made mandatory
a concrete follow-up benchmark/adoption decision is recorded
